source_excerpt: The timeless Telugu musical drama 'Sankarabharanam' is preparing for another theatrical outing, more than four decades after its original release. The 1980 classic will return to cinemas worldwide in November with an upgraded digital presentation. The restored version will feature 4K Ultra HD visuals and 7.1 Surround Sound. Sreelal Devaraj, who supervised the new digital version, confirmed the re-release plans to ETimes.Sreelal Devara exclusively shared the update with ETimes. He informed,"The theatrical comeback is planned across Malayalam and Tamil markets worldwide. The new version has been prepared with enhanced visual clarity and an upgraded sound format. The 4K Ultra HD presentation aims to bring greater detail to the film's original visuals."Meanwhile, the 7.1 Surround Sound mix is expected to offer a more immersive experience. A. S. Dinesh and Manu Shivan are the PRO's.Written and directed by K. Viswanath, 'Sankarabharanam' examined the cultural relationship between Indian classical music and Western pop music. The story brought together characters from different generations and backgrounds. It also explored the challenges faced by a respected musician in a society where his artistic values were increasingly overlooked. J. V. Somayajulu and Manju Bhargavi played the lead rolesJ. V. Somayajulu portrayed Shankara Sastry, an acclaimed classical singer whose music deeply influences Tulasi. Manju Bhargavi played Tulasi, the daughter of a prostitute who wishes to dedicate herself to the musician. However, her mother has different plans for her future.Chandra Mohan appeared as Kameswara Rao, while Rajyalakshmi played Sarada. The supporting cast included Tulasi as Shankaram, Allu Ramalingaiah as Madhava and Nirmalamma as Bamma. Their performances helped bring the film's central relationships and conflicts to life.K. V. Mahadevan and S. P. Balasubrahmanyam created musical magicThe soundtrack, composed by K. V. Mahadevan, remains one of the film's most celebrated aspects. S. P. Balasubrahmanyam's vocals gave several compositions their enduring appeal. Among them, 'Sankaraa... Naadasareera Paraa' continues to be cherished by generations of music lovers.National recognition strengthened the film's legacy'Sankarabharanam' received the National Film Award for Best Popular Film. In 1980, it was also honoured with a Gold Medal presented by then President of India Neelam Sanjiva Reddy.
